items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Brock Mumford; the name is only introduced by the interviewer.

ctx.x: Yes, yes. He was of a dark complex with straight hair. Frankie Doosan. He came from Algiers too, Professor. Why, I know the whole family. I'm trying to think of all of them. But I just can't think it's been so long in no years. Frankie Doosan.

A banjo player, but I don't think he was from Algiers, the Brock Mumford. Who? Mumford, Brock. Brock? And then there was the Lorenzo Stahl. Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. But they were from over on the other side, uptown on the other side of the river.

Yeah, well I knew Lorenzo Stahl for a pretty period too there, but he played with us once too. I think he went up on this trip when you said about, oh, his brother coming through the cane. Uh-huh. I think Lorenzo Stahl was with him. He was with Oliver. Oh, he was?
